prompt: A positive binary32 bit pattern has an all-zero exponent and only the last fraction bit set. What is it?

options.explanation: A normal value needs a nonzero exponent field and the implicit leading one.
Correct. The zero hidden bit and lowest fraction bit encode the smallest positive subnormal.
Zero needs an all-zero fraction as well as an all-zero exponent.

workedExample: The exponent field selects the subnormal rule. Its hidden bit is zero, but the fraction is nonzero, so this is not zero. With only the lowest fraction position set, no smaller positive nonzero pattern exists in binary32.
